protocol:
1. Set up a PCR assembly area with a green ice bucket containing chilled labeled microtubes, including tubes labeled FP, DNA, and H2O; place PCR tubes/strips in yellow and white tube racks and have a micropipette and pipette tips available.

2. Keep the labeled reagent tubes on ice and remove each required tube one at a time for use during reaction setup.

3. Mix the chilled reagent tubes by brief hand flicking/inversion before adding their contents to the reaction.

4. Assemble the reaction in a clear PCR tube/strip held in a yellow rack by pipetting aliquots from the chilled labeled tubes into the PCR vessel.

5. Return reagent tubes to the ice bucket between additions to keep them cold.

6. Cap the assembled PCR tube/strip after all visible additions are complete.

7. Briefly spin down the capped PCR tube/strip in a benchtop mini-centrifuge with a blue rotor to collect liquid at the bottom of the tube.

8. Load the capped PCR tube/strip into a Bio-Rad T100 thermal cycler and close the heated lid.

9. On the Bio-Rad T100 thermal cycler touchscreen, open the saved protocols menu and select the saved protocol named “PHANTA.”

10. Start the “PHANTA” thermal cycler run with the reaction volume set to 20 µL; the display shows approximately 38 min remaining, lid heating, and visible temperature stages including 95°C, 98°C, 72°C, and a 12°C hold.
